newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain seeks arrest of Argentine ex-president.
newsitem.headline: Spain seeks arrest of Argentine ex-president.

text.p: A Spanish judge issued an international arrest warrant on Tuesday for former Argentine military president Leopoldo Galtieri for his alleged role in the killings of three Spaniards during Argentina's "dirty war".

National High Court Judge Baltasar Garzon, who is investigating the disappearances of about 300 Spanish nationals in Argentina from 1976 to 1983, said he was asking Interpol to take Galtieri into custody if he leaves his homeland.
"An order of imprisonment against Galtieri has been issued," Garzon told Reuters.

The 70-year-old retired general, who led the ruling junta from 1980 to 1982 and ordered the failed invasion of the Falkland (Malvinas) Islands held by Britain, lives in Argentina. The Argentine government has so far refused to cooperate with Garzon's investigation.
Angel Garcia Castillejo, an attorney for the victims' families, said: "This detention order is the first step in placing responsibility for these horrible crimes."

The allegations against Galtieri arise from Garzon's investigation of the Argentine military's campaign of terror against suspected leftists in which more than 14,000 people were abducted and murdered. This is the first arrest warrant Garzon has issued in his year-long investigation.

Garzon's investigation linked Galtieri to the disappearances of Victor Labrador and his two sons who vanished in Argentina in 1976. The bodies of the father and one son were discovered with signs of torture. The other son's body has not been found, but Garzon alleged he was also killed.
Garzon said in his warrant that Galtieri, then an army general, had ordered the killings on the grounds that the victims were leftist extremists.

"Galtieri played an active role in all these acts along with other military chiefs, in the creation and development of a state of terror and genocide and as one of those who orchestrated murders and related kidnappings," the arrest warrant said.
Garzon, who has tried some of Spain's most notorious criminal cases, wants Galtieri brought to justice in Spain. Spanish law does not allow for a defendant to be tried in absentia.
But without cooperation from the Argentine government, Galtieri will remain beyond the reach of Spanish authorities unless he leaves Argentina and is detained and extradited from a third country.
